description: The bar chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published per year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the number of languages they cover, as presented in the paper “The Unseen Targets of Hate — A Systematic Review of Hateful Communication Datasets.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of datasets,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 100, with major gridlines at 10¹ and 10². The horizontal axis represents the year, spanning from 2012 to 2022. A legend titled “Languages” indicates that blue bars represent datasets covering one language, orange bars represent datasets covering two languages, and light gray bars represent datasets covering three or more languages — though only one such dataset appears, in 2022. The data show a general upward trend in dataset publication over time: from 2012 to 2015, only single-language datasets were published, each with 1–3 datasets per year. Starting in 2016, the number of single-language datasets increased sharply, reaching 10 in 2016, 20 in 2017, 30 in 2018, 40 in 2019, 100 in 2020, and peaking at approximately 120 in 2021. Multi-language datasets begin appearing in 2017 (one 2-language dataset), with small numbers in 2018 (one 2-language), 2019 (one 2-language), 2020 (one 2-language), and 2021 (one 2-language). In 2022, there is a notable shift: the number of single-language datasets drops to approximately 30 (light blue bar), while a single 3-language dataset appears (light gray bar) and one 2-language dataset remains (orange bar). The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of single-language datasets until 2021, followed by a diversification in 2022 toward multi-language resources.
